one_line: OpenAI raises funds, expands API, while safety and policy restrictions tighten worldwide.

themes.title: OpenAI seeks $30 billion funding
themes.text: OpenAI is negotiating a private funding round of up to $30 billion that would value the company at $1.25 trillion pre‑money, led by Coatue and investors from the United Arab Emirates.

stories.headline: OpenAI seeks up to $30 billion funding at $1.25 trillion valuation ahead of IPO

themes.title: OpenAI launches multimodal Decisions API
themes.text: OpenAI made its Decisions API generally available on Oct 22 2026, charging $0.10 per million input tokens, adding voice and visual modalities, and delivering latency around 150 ms, up to ten‑times faster than standard GPT‑6 Luna calls.

stories.headline: OpenAI launches Decisions API with voice, visual inputs at $0.10 per million tokens

themes.title: AI safety concerns after firings, breaches
themes.text: OpenAI terminated three safety researchers after an internal investigation said they leaked internal model designs via disappearing Signal chats. Microsoft reported that China‑aligned hackers used the open‑source AI framework ARTEX to infiltrate about 2,250 organizations, gaining privileged cloud access in some cases within three hours.

stories.headline: OpenAI fires three safety researchers over alleged leak of internal model designs
Chinese hackers used AI agents to breach ConnectWise and access 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants

themes.title: Governments and banks restrict AI tools
themes.text: Swedish government ministries have prohibited staff from using ChatGPT and Claude on work computers, requiring Microsoft Copilot as the only approved AI tool. Major U.S. banks including JPMorgan Chase, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, Wells Fargo and Citi are restricting or blocking third‑party AI agents from accessing customer accounts after detecting unauthorized activity. Meta’s updated commercial terms, effective Oct. 30 2026, allow business accounts to authorize the company to scrape content from associated websites, including news sites, for AI training.

stories.headline: Swedish government offices ban ChatGPT and Claude, require Microsoft Copilot
Major US banks block third‑party AI agents from customer accounts
Meta’s new commercial terms could let it scrape news sites for AI training
